title: How to reduce heat damage when styling your hair
excerpt: Changes to drying, tool temperature and styling frequency can reduce avoidable stress on your hair.
primaryKeyword: how to prevent heat damage to hair
body: Repeated high temperatures can leave hair brittle and more prone to breakage. Dermatologists recommend reducing heat exposure, allowing hair to air-dry when practical and using hot tools on a low or medium setting. Read the American Academy of Dermatology guidance on styling without damage.
tip1: Let hair air-dry until it is partly dry before using a blow-dryer.
tip2: Choose a low or medium heat setting rather than the maximum temperature.
tip3: Use a heat-protectant product labelled for your tool and hair type, following its directions.
tip4: Keep hot tools moving and avoid holding them against one section for longer than needed.
tip5: Give hair breaks between heat-styling sessions. Ask a qualified professional or dermatologist about persistent breakage or scalp symptoms.

title: BIAB vs gel extensions: which nail service should you choose?
excerpt: BIAB and gel extensions serve different purposes. Compare natural-nail support, added length, maintenance and removal before booking.
body:
If you are comparing BIAB and gel extensions in Dubai, start with the result you want rather than the product name. BIAB (builder-in-a-bottle) is generally used as a builder overlay on the natural nail. Gel extensions are designed to add length or change the nail shape. Products and techniques vary, so confirm exactly what the salon offers.

What BIAB is designed to do

BIAB is commonly applied over the natural nail to create a structured overlay. It may suit someone who wants a reinforced finish while keeping their existing length. The result depends on the product, application and condition of the natural nail.

When gel extensions may make more sense

Gel extensions are an option when you want additional length or a more substantial shape change. The technician should assess your natural nails, discuss a manageable length and explain maintenance and removal.

Questions to ask before booking

  • Is this an overlay or will it add length?
  • How is the product removed: soaking, filing or both?
  • What maintenance interval is recommended?
  • What should I do if lifting or discomfort appears?

Choose around your nails and routine

For short natural nails and a structured finish, ask whether BIAB is suitable. If length is the priority, discuss gel extensions and realistic upkeep. A consultation at a nail salon in Al Barsha can match the method to your nail condition and routine.

For general nail-health advice, see the American Academy of Dermatology guidance on reducing artificial-nail damage.

title: Brow lamination aftercare: five habits for the first 48 hours
excerpt: Follow the specific aftercare instructions from your brow professional while freshly styled brows settle.
body: Aftercare varies with the products and process used. Before leaving your appointment, ask your brow professional how long to keep the area dry and which products to avoid. Contact a healthcare professional if you experience unexpected irritation or swelling.
tip1: Follow the aftercare card or instructions supplied by your brow professional; timing differs between systems.
tip2: If your technician advises keeping brows dry for a set period, avoid steam, swimming and direct water during that window.
tip3: Avoid exfoliating acids, retinoids, strong cleansers or unapproved brow products until your technician says they are suitable.
tip4: Do not rub, brush aggressively or reshape the brows while the treatment is settling.
tip5: After the initial aftercare period, use only the conditioning product recommended for your treatment and brush gently.

title: Russian manicure: what to ask before booking the service
excerpt: Understand the technique, tool handling, cuticle approach and hygiene questions to discuss before choosing a Russian manicure.
body:
A Russian manicure is commonly described as a detailed dry manicure that uses an e-file and specialised bits to refine the nail area. The term is used for different service variations; the result depends on the technician’s training, technique and assessment of your nails. It is not simply a standard manicure with a different polish.

Understand what the appointment includes

Ask the salon to explain each step. Find out whether the treatment includes e-file work around the cuticle area, nail shaping, product application and removal of existing enhancements. Discuss a gentler alternative if you do not want detailed cuticle work.

Ask about tools and hygiene

Ask how reusable metal instruments are cleaned and sterilised, how single-use items are handled and whether tools are prepared for each client. Dubai Municipality’s Ideal Salon Technical Guidelines provide a local reference for salon standards.

Is it right for every nail?

No single manicure technique is appropriate for every person or nail condition. Tell the technician if your nails are thin, damaged or sensitive. Speak up if you feel pain or burning; detailed cuticle work should not be painful.

Make the decision before the appointment

Choose this service only after you understand the method, the technician’s experience and the hygiene process. If you prefer a simpler approach, ask about a classic manicure or another option that matches your comfort level.

title: Simple ways to keep a pedicure looking neat between visits
excerpt: Moisturising, sensible footwear and gentle nail care help maintain a tidy pedicure between appointments.
body: These are cosmetic maintenance suggestions, not treatment for foot or nail conditions. If you notice pain, swelling, discolouration or a persistent change in a nail, seek advice from a qualified healthcare professional.
tip1: Apply a foot moisturiser regularly, concentrating on dry areas while avoiding slippery residue on the soles.
tip2: Wear shoes with enough room at the toes so nails are not repeatedly pressed against the front of the shoe.
tip3: Keep toenails at a comfortable length and avoid cutting deeply into the corners.
tip4: Dry feet carefully after showering, including between the toes, before putting on socks or closed shoes.
tip5: Do not cut or forcefully push back cuticles. The American Academy of Dermatology explains why cuticles help protect against infection.

title: How to choose a nail shape that works with your hands and routine
excerpt: Almond, oval, square and squoval nails create different finishes. Use length, natural nail shape and daily tasks to guide your choice.
body:
The best nail shape is the one that suits your natural nail length, the finish you prefer and what your hands do every day. A reference photo helps, but the same shape can look different on different nail beds and lengths. Your technician can show you a practical version before shaping all ten nails.

Almond: tapered with a soft point

Almond nails narrow towards the tip and have a rounded point. They can create an elongated look, but usually need enough free edge to form the taper. On very short nails, ask whether a softer oval would achieve a similar effect.

Square: straight sides and a flat tip

Square nails have a crisp, straight edge. They create a structured finish, especially when there is enough length to keep the corners balanced. If your nails catch on fabric or you work with your hands, discuss softening the corners.

Oval: a rounded everyday shape

Oval nails follow a curved outline and can be practical at shorter lengths. They are useful if you prefer a softer edge without a pointed tip.

Squoval: a compromise between square and oval

Squoval combines straighter sides with gently rounded corners. It keeps some of the square look while reducing sharp corners that may catch.

Choose for comfort, not only the photograph

Tell your nail technician how long you want to keep the nails, whether you type or handle equipment frequently and whether you prefer a natural or extended length. A nail shape should feel comfortable in daily use as well as look balanced in a photo.

title: What to do after a waxing appointment
excerpt: Keep post-wax care simple and follow your therapist’s advice on heat, friction and products for the treated area.
body: Skin can look temporarily red or feel sensitive after waxing. The American Academy of Dermatology recommends soothing the skin and avoiding hot baths or showers after waxing. Seek medical advice if redness or swelling persists or worsens. Reference: AAD waxing guidance.
tip1: Avoid very hot showers, steam rooms and hot baths immediately after waxing if the area feels warm or sensitive.
tip2: Choose loose, breathable clothing to reduce rubbing on freshly waxed skin.
tip3: Use a gentle moisturiser that you already know your skin tolerates; avoid fragranced or strong active products if the area is irritated.
tip4: Do not scrub, exfoliate or repeatedly touch the treated area while it is settling.
tip5: If redness or swelling lasts more than two days, becomes painful or worsens, seek advice from a qualified healthcare professional.

title: Haircut consultation: how to explain the layers and face-framing you want
excerpt: Bring useful reference photos and explain your styling routine so your stylist can adapt layers and face-framing to your hair.
body:
A haircut reference photo is useful, but it rarely tells the whole story. The person in the picture may have different hair density, texture, length or styling habits. A focused consultation helps your stylist understand which parts of the look matter and what can realistically be recreated with your hair.

Bring more than one reference

Choose two or three images that show the shape from different angles. Point out the detail you like: face-framing pieces, movement around the ends, a softer outline or a particular fringe. Also show one image of a result you do not want. This is often clearer than saying only that you want “more layers”.

Explain your everyday styling routine

Tell your stylist how much time you spend styling, whether you air-dry, use a blow-dryer or wear your hair tied back. Layers that look defined after a professional blow-dry may behave differently when left to dry naturally.

Discuss length before the first cut

Agree on the shortest point around the face and the amount of length to remove from the back. Ask the stylist to show where the layers will sit and whether they can be adjusted if you want a more subtle result.

Share your hair history

Mention previous chemical services, colour, extensions and breakage concerns. These details help the stylist plan the cut and finish around your hair’s condition.

Leave with a manageable shape

The best haircut is not just the one that photographs well in the salon. It should work with your texture, routine and preferred level of maintenance. A clear consultation gives your stylist a better brief before the scissors come out.

title: How to detangle wet hair with less breakage
excerpt: Use the right timing and a gentle detangling method for your hair texture instead of pulling through knots.
body: Wet hair can be more vulnerable to breakage, but the best detangling method depends on texture. The American Academy of Dermatology advises people with straight hair to let it dry somewhat before gently combing, while tightly curled or textured hair is often best detangled when damp with a wide-tooth comb. Reference: AAD guidance on styling without damage.
tip1: Do not pull a brush from roots to ends through a knot. Separate the tangle gently with your fingers first.
tip2: For straight hair, allow it to dry a little before using a wide-tooth comb.
tip3: For tightly curled or textured hair, detangle while damp and use conditioner or a suitable detangling product for slip.
tip4: Work in small sections, starting at the ends and moving gradually towards the roots.
tip5: If the comb repeatedly catches, stop and add more conditioner or detangler rather than forcing it through.

title: How to prepare for a professional makeup appointment in Dubai
excerpt: A clear brief, realistic reference images and a familiar pre-appointment routine help your makeup artist plan the finish you want.
body:
A professional makeup appointment works best when the artist understands the event, the finish you like and how you normally wear makeup. A reference photo is helpful, but lighting, filters and the model’s features can change how a look appears. Use the image to explain the details you like rather than expecting an exact copy.

Share the event and timing

Tell the artist whether the makeup is for a daytime event, evening function, photoshoot or wedding. Mention the venue, start time and whether you will be outdoors. This helps the artist discuss coverage, finish and touch-ups.

Bring useful references

Choose one or two clear images and identify the elements you want: eye definition, lip colour, complexion finish or blush placement. Also explain anything you dislike, such as heavy lashes or a very matte base.

Keep skin preparation familiar

Use products your skin already tolerates before the appointment. Avoid experimenting with strong exfoliants or unfamiliar treatments immediately beforehand, especially if you are prone to sensitivity. Arrive with a clean face unless the artist advises otherwise.

Discuss sensitivities and product preferences

Tell the artist about known allergies, contact-lens use, skin sensitivities and products you prefer not to use. For medical skin concerns, seek advice from a healthcare professional rather than relying on makeup to treat them.

Agree on the finish

Confirm whether you want a natural, defined or dramatic result, and ask how long the appointment will take. A good brief gives the artist room to adapt the inspiration to your features and the occasion.

title: 2026 haircare report highlights scalp-first routines and prevention-led care
excerpt: A Cosmetics Business report drawing on Circana and Worldpanel data describes a shift towards scalp care, prevention and targeted hair treatments.
body:
Cosmetics Business published its 2026 Hair Care Trend Report coverage on 7 October, describing a shift from reactive repair towards prevention-led routines and greater attention to scalp health. The article reports that prestige haircare sales in Europe grew 24% to €1.2 billion in the 12 months ending August 2026, citing Circana. It also cites Worldpanel by Numerator data showing UK scalp treatment sales up 12% for the year ending 9 August 2026.

Scalp care and targeted products gain attention

The report discusses scalp treatments, hair serums, bond-building products and newer formats such as scalp exfoliants and dry shampoo mists. These are market signals from Europe and the UK, not UAE salon sales figures. They indicate product-development direction, but do not prove that every trend suits every hair type.

What clients can take from the report

Identify the concern you want help with—such as dryness, breakage, styling build-up or colour maintenance—and ask for a routine that addresses it. Do not treat a trend ingredient or scalp product as a medical solution for hair loss or scalp disease.
